verse: Genesis 1:26 (NKJV): Then God said, 'Let Us make man in Our image, according to Our likeness; let them have dominion...'
teaching:
From the beginning, God's intention for humanity was not merely existence, but representation. When God created man in His image and likeness, He placed within humanity a divine purpose: to express His nature and exercise His authority over creation.

However, through the fall of Adam, mankind lost the consciousness of this divine identity and became dominated by fear, limitation, and the influence of the fallen world. Humanity moved from a position of authority into a position of struggle. But the Gospel reveals the restoration of God's original purpose through Jesus Christ.

Through the finished work of Christ, the believer has been completely restored to God's eternal plan. Jesus did not come merely to forgive sins; He came to bring humanity back into fellowship with God and restore the believer's true identity. In Christ, we are no longer slaves to sin, fear, circumstances, or the limitations of natural reasoning. We have received the very life and nature of God through the New Creation.

Dominion begins with revelation. A believer who does not understand his identity will constantly be controlled by external circumstances. But when your spirit is enlightened by the knowledge of who you are in Christ, you begin to live from a position of victory rather than from a place of defeat.

The authority of the believer does not come from human ability, education, wealth, or influence. It comes from union with Christ and the indwelling presence of the Holy Spirit. The same life that raised Jesus from the dead now operates within the believer, giving wisdom, strength, and spiritual authority.

Walking in dominion means allowing God's Word to govern your thoughts, decisions, and actions. It means refusing to be ruled by fear, emotions, or the reports of the natural world. Instead, you respond from the reality of God's Kingdom and the finished work of Jesus Christ.

A person walking in dominion understands that they are a carrier of God's presence. Wherever God has placed you — in your family, workplace, ministry, or society — you are called to bring Kingdom influence. You are not waiting for circumstances to change before you walk in victory; you walk in victory because Christ has already overcome.

Never forget: dominion is not something you achieve through human striving. It is a reality revealed through your identity in Christ. As you grow in the knowledge of the Word, your consciousness changes, your words align with God's truth, and your life begins to demonstrate the authority that belongs to every New Creation.
goldenNugget: Dominion is not something you struggle to achieve; it is a reality you discover through your identity in Christ.
prayerDeclaration: Father, thank You for restoring me through the finished work of Jesus Christ. I receive revelation of my identity as a New Creation and I walk today in the authority, wisdom, and power of the Holy Spirit. My thoughts, words, and actions reflect Your Kingdom. I am not controlled by circumstances, but I live from the victory Christ has already accomplished. In Jesus' name, Amen.
